record_identity.title: Cruise autonomous vehicle moved away after San Francisco police traffic stop

incident_identity.date_basis: Date follows the reviewed registry or primary occurrence record; no narrower time is inferred.

summary: San Francisco police stopped an unoccupied Cruise autonomous Chevrolet Bolt after officers observed a lighting issue. Video and subsequent reporting showed the vehicle initially stopped, then moved farther down the road before stopping again with hazard lights. Cruise said the vehicle yielded to the police vehicle and then moved to the nearest safe location. Police reported contacting the remote operator before a maintenance team took control. City representatives later met with Cruise about the incident. In its revised May 2022 filing, San Francisco said that ordinary moving-violation citation procedures assumed a human driver and generally could not be used against driverless vehicles, although fix-it, camera and parking citation routes remained available. That was the City's contemporary legal assessment, not a finding of a new violation by this vehicle.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: San Francisco police stopped an unoccupied Cruise autonomous Chevrolet Bolt after officers observed a lighting issue. Video and subsequent reporting showed the vehicle initially stopped, then moved farther down the road before stopping again with hazard lights. Cruise said the vehicle yielded to the police vehicle and then moved to the nearest safe location. The local report separately preserves police and provider statements. The official city filing documents a later meeting and video-review opportunity. It does not establish a command to remain stationary or loss of a feasible admissible route. San Francisco's revised 24 May 2022 submission to the California Public Utilities Commission also addressed a distinct legal enforcement gap highlighted by this stop. The City said Vehicle Code sections 40500(a) and 40504 generally required identifying a human driver and obtaining a signed notice to appear for ordinary moving violations. It noted alternative routes for certain fix-it, red-light-camera and parking citations. The submission did not establish a separately proven moving violation in this traffic stop or determine the legal position after May 2022.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The vehicle’s movement and subsequent stop are documented, but the internal process trace available to investigators is not established. The external assessment does not infer flight from police, a safety-system failure or a general right to move after a stop. Harm Impact: Police contacted the remote operator and a maintenance team took control after the lighting fault. The reported correction and local operational intervention support routine local workflow impairment. No ticket or reported injury is not affirmative evidence of no operational harm. The City's May 2022 position also identified an institutional limitation: moving-violation citation procedures assumed a human driver able to receive and sign a notice. That legal-process gap affected oversight of driverless deployment but is not, on this evidence, a breach of an AI-system Fidelity Class or a conclusion that all AV citations were impossible.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: Autonomous vehicles need legible, predictable protocols for exceptional human authority such as police stops. Even a movement intended to improve roadside safety can create confusion if officers cannot understand the vehicle's state, communicate with it or know where it will stop next. Oversight also requires legally addressable recipients for enforcement actions. The 2022 City filing illustrates how conventional driver-identification and citation procedures may fail to map directly onto driverless systems, independently of the vehicle's observed stop behaviour.
assessment_boundaries: Cruise's explanation that the vehicle moved to the nearest safe location is preserved as the company's account.
The evidence does not establish the vehicle's internal perception or planning state.
No injury or collision is reported. The separate remote-operator and maintenance intervention supports local operational harm.
The occurrence does not determine whether the lighting issue or vehicle response violated a particular legal requirement.

San Francisco's moving-violation citation concern is a May 2022 institutional legal assessment, subject to exceptions for fix-it, camera and parking citations; it is not a conclusion about current California law or proof that this specific vehicle committed a legally established moving violation.
